title: Parameter Estimation in Land Surface Models: Challenges and Opportunities With Data Assimilation and Machine Learning
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
testbed_rationale: This paper is a review article summarizing challenges, data assimilation methods, and machine learning opportunities for parameter estimation in land surface models; it does not produce or provide a unified, accessible ML benchmark dataset.
pain_points: High computational cost of running complex land surface models for large ensembles or iterative MCMC algorithms.
Curse of dimensionality due to many vegetation (PFTs) and soil texture classes.
Equifinality where different parameter combinations yield identical model fits.
Difficulty in characterizing model structural error versus observation error / data biases.
Observation error correlations (spatial/temporal) typically omitted or unknown.
Constructing and maintaining adjoint or tangent linear models in legacy Fortran code bases.
Spin-up and historical period computational expense required to constrain slow-acting soil carbon pools.
Mismatch of spatial resolution and forward representation between satellite observations and model grid cells.
extraction_notes: This is a comprehensive review paper resulting from the AIMES Land DA Working Group and ILMF. As stated in the Data Availability Statement: 'This article discusses the challenges and priorities in the field of parameter estimation for land DA, and the opportunities offered by ML—it does not include the specific use of any particular software or results involving specific data products.' Therefore, no discrete dataset objects are created.
